title: Asynchronous KV Cache Prefetching — Active L2 Prefetch for PagedAttention
summary_zh: Alibaba 對 vLLM v0.10.2 的 PagedAttention decode kernel 做了約 10 行的增補式修改：在計算當前 KV block 時，用 PTX 指令 cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2.global 主動把下一個 KV block（block_idx + NUM_WARPS）從 HBM 預取進 L2，以隱藏記憶體延遲。在 H20 上回報注意力 kernel 約 2.15×、端到端最高約 1.97×。對我們「Worth the Bytes?」的論點而言這是對抗性上界：它的 L2 增益來自主動、kernel 內、軟體發起地預取高重用的 KV-cache，而非我們所量化的被動、跨 kernel 的 activation 殘留——因此幾乎 0% 屬於我們界定的機制，反而強化了 <0.65% 的上界。
summary_en: Alibaba's ~10-line additive patch to vLLM v0.10.2's PagedAttention decode kernel issues the PTX instruction cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2.global to actively stage the next KV block (block_idx + NUM_WARPS) from HBM into L2 while the current block is being computed, hiding memory latency. Reports ~2.15× attention-kernel and up to ~1.97× e2e on H20. For our "Worth the Bytes?" claim this is the adversarial upper bound: its L2 win comes from active, intra-kernel, software-issued prefetch of the high-reuse KV-cache, not the passive, inter-kernel activation residency we bound — so ~0% of its gain is the mechanism we quantify, which sharpens rather than contradicts the <0.65% bound.
